turns.question: 6061 알루미늄 브래킷이 SPCC 브래킷보다 내구(피로) 시험 불합격률이 높아? 각각 불합격률 알려줘.
turns.answer:
네. 6061 알루미늄 브래킷의 피로시험 불합격률은 약 33%로, SPCC 브래킷(16%)의 두 배 정도입니다.

| 재질 | 피로시험을 받은 브래킷 | 불합격 이력이 있는 브래킷 | 불합격률 |
|---|---|---|---|
| AL6061-T6 | 42개 | 14개 | **33.3%** |
| SPCC | 50개 | 8개 | **16.0%** |

**계산 기준**
- 시험 리포트 건수가 아니라 **부품 수**로 센 값입니다. 피로시험을 한 번 이상 받은 브래킷이 분모이고, 그중 불합격 리포트가 하나라도 있는 브래킷이 분자입니다.
- **모든 리비전**의 시험을 포함했습니다. 예전 리비전에서 불합격했다가 다음 리비전에서 고친 부품도 불합격으로 들어가 있어서, 지금 해결되지 않은 문제의 비율과는 다를 수 있습니다.
- 조건부 합격은 불합격에 넣지 않았습니다.

원하시면 이어서 확인해 드릴 수 있습니다.
- 현재 리비전 기준으로 아직 해결되지 않은 불합격만 다시 계산
- 불합격한 브래킷 목록(AL 14개, SPCC 8개)과 리포트에 적힌 불합격 원인

turns.question: Which brackets changed material between revisions? From what to what, and why?
turns.answer:
I found three brackets whose change notices record a material change. In all three, the records give the new material but **not the original rev A material**, so I can't tell you what they changed from.

| Part | Change | Changed to | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| BR-76459 (front fascia bracket, 190×90) | Rev A → B [ECO-431230] | SPFH590 (steel sheet) | The notice doesn't say. Rev A bent permanently at 12.6 kN in a static load test [TR-163650]. |
| BR-32787 (202×70) | Rev A → B [ECO-143744] | SPFH590 | The notice doesn't say. Rev A bent permanently at 2.9 kN, short of the 5 kN target [TR-139121]. |
| BR-43365 (pulley bracket, 236×122) | Rev A → B [ECO-803381] | SUS304 (stainless) | Stated in the notice: rev A failed salt spray with red rust at the weld bead at 168 h, short of the 240 h target [TR-119354]. |

**Why: stated vs. inferred**
- **BR-43365:** the change notice itself names the salt spray failure as the reason.
- **BR-76459 and BR-32787:** the static failure is my reading, not a stated reason. In both, rev A failed static load testing before the change notice date. This suggests the switch was a strength fix, but the notices don't say so.

**Did the change work?** In all three, the new material passes the test that rev A failed:
- **BR-76459** rev B passed 20 kN static [TR-641818], fatigue at 1000k cycles [TR-979402] and 480 h salt spray [TR-911017].
- **BR-32787** rev C held 5 kN without deformation [TR-993437]. Rev C only clarified tolerances [ECO-359206]. Rev B, which got the material change, has no test on record.
- **BR-43365** rev B passed 240 h salt spray [TR-127966].

Many other bracket corrosion problems were fixed by adding zinc-nickel coating instead of changing material (for example BR-26936 [ECO-156903]). Those aren't counted here.

My searches went through bracket change notices for material changes; these three are the only ones I found.

turns.question: Do 6061 aluminum brackets fail durability (fatigue) testing more often than SPCC brackets? Give the failure rate for each.
turns.answer:
Yes. Among brackets that have been fatigue (durability) tested, 6061 aluminum brackets have failed about twice as often as SPCC brackets.

| Material | Brackets fatigue-tested | Brackets with a fatigue failure (any revision) | Failure rate | Failure still on the current revision |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AL6061-T6 | 42 | 14 | **33%** | 9 (21%) |
| SPCC | 50 | 8 | **16%** | 4 (8%) |

How these numbers work:
- **Counted by part, not by test.** A bracket counts as failed if it has at least one failed fatigue report. I don't have the total number of fatigue tests, so these aren't failures per test.
- **The first rate includes old revisions.** Some of those failures were on earlier revisions that were later fixed. The last column counts only parts whose failure is on the current revision, meaning the problem is still open: 9 for aluminum and 4 for SPCC. Both last-column rates use all tested brackets as the denominator, since I didn't count how many were tested on their current revision.
- **The groups are small** (42 and 50 parts). The gap is consistent, but bracket designs differ between the two groups, so this shows a pattern, not proof that the material causes it.
- **These are database counts, so there are no individual report ids to cite.**

I can list the failed brackets for either material and pull their failure notes, such as where they cracked and what changes were made. That would show whether the aluminum failures come from the material or from the designs.

turns.question: Which released 6061 aluminum bracket is the heaviest, and who supplies it, at what lead time and unit cost?

The heaviest released AL6061-T6 bracket is **BR-50223 rev A**, "Bracket 778x629 (Faucet)", at **141,692 g (about 141.7 kg)**.

- **Supplier:** Supplier 03
- **Lead time:** 4 weeks
- **Unit cost:** 1,105,760 KRW

**Details:**
- **Size and mass:** It measures 777.9 × 628.7 × 606.4 mm, with a CAD volume of about 52.5 million mm³. That volume times the density of 6061 matches the recorded mass, so the weight looks right.
- **Next heaviest:** BR-79073 at 59,265 g and BR-28206 at 25,950 g. That puts BR-50223 more than twice the weight of any other.
- **Program and owner:** Program P1, owned by Chassis Design. Rev A was released 2024-10-01 and has no change notices.
- **Test history:** It passed its fatigue test on rev A: 1000k cycles with no fracture, BR-50223 [TR-151090].

**One thing to check:** The part name says "Faucet" and its fill ratio is only 0.18. That doesn't sound like a normal bracket, so it may be misclassified in PLM. It's worth confirming with Chassis Design before relying on it.

turns.question: Did any part that looks like BR-66254 fail fatigue testing? For the ones that were fixed and are released now, who is the supplier?
turns.answer:
Yes. Two parts that look like BR-66254 failed fatigue testing on rev A, and both passed after a fix in rev B. Only one of them is released: **BR-19198, and its supplier is Supplier 04** (2,240 KRW, 4-week lead time).

**BR-19198** (Bracket 96x83, AL6061-T6, 0.881 shape similarity, about 1.6× the size of BR-66254), released
- Rev A failed fatigue: a crack at the bolt hole after 509k of the 1000k target cycles [TR-381830].
- The fix was a wall thickness increase from 2.0 to 3.0 mm, A→B [ECO-835133].
- Rev B passed fatigue at 1000k cycles with no fracture [TR-881948] and passed static strength [TR-570744].
- Rev B was released 2024-10-25.

**BR-83689** (Bracket 250x150, AL6061-T6, 0.896 shape similarity, about 4.2× the size), fixed but still In Work
- Rev A failed fatigue: cracking at the bolt hole after 90k of the 200k target cycles [TR-236803].
- It got the same fix, wall thickness 2.0 to 3.0 mm [ECO-941845].
- Rev B passed fatigue [TR-225469] and static [TR-863076].
- It is not released, and the ERP has no supplier for it.

No other part in the top 20 shape matches has a fatigue failure on record. Both failures were cracks at the bolt hole on 2.0 mm walls. BR-66254 is the same material (AL6061-T6) and has no test reports yet, so the bolt-hole area and wall thickness are worth checking early.

- 공급사는 부품 카드에 Supplier 04로 등록되어 있습니다.

turns.question: Has any fix failed? I mean a part that was revised to fix a failed test but still fails that same test on the new revision.
turns.answer:
I found no case where a fix failed. None of the parts I checked was revised to fix a failed test and then failed that same test again on the new revision.

**What I checked:** 151 parts have a failed test on their current revision. Of those, I opened the full history of every part that has been revised to rev B or C, in Body, Block, Plate, Bracket, Cover, Flange and Housing, plus 18 of the 22 Beams.

**Not checked:** 4 Beams, 2 Washers, 2 Shafts and 1 Pin. The search results were cut off before showing them, so I can't rule them out yet.

**What I found instead:** the fix worked, but the new revision failed a different test. In 9 cases a revision made to fix a failure passed the retest, and a different test then failed:
- **BM-13492:** a rev A static failure [TR-236560] led to thicker walls [ECO-933710]. Rev B passes static [TR-380154] but fails fatigue with a crack at the fillet at 554k cycles [TR-187862].
- **BM-46007:** a rev A static failure [TR-859665] led to thicker walls [ECO-554364]. Rev B passes static [TR-839627] but fails fatigue, cracking at 391k of 500k cycles [TR-521914].
- **BM-76654:** a fatigue failure [TR-516252] led to thicker walls [ECO-153874]. Rev B passes fatigue [TR-983426] but fails static, deforming at 3.2 kN against a 5 kN requirement [TR-472612].
- **BR-37660:** a fatigue failure [TR-888735] led to thicker walls [ECO-148761]. Rev B passes fatigue [TR-883594] but fails salt spray [TR-861742].
- **PL-81760:** a fatigue failure [TR-942738] led to thicker walls [ECO-218303]. Rev B passes fatigue [TR-551588] but fails salt spray at the weld bead [TR-995811].
- **BR-91781:** a salt spray failure [TR-272150] led to an insulating washer [ECO-177690]. Rev B passes salt spray [TR-888912] but fails static [TR-393469].
- **BR-97230:** a salt spray failure [TR-355936] led to zinc-nickel plating [ECO-912494]. Rev B passes salt spray [TR-485362] but fails static [TR-648181].
- **CV-81887:** a rattle (NVH) failure [TR-609173] led to an added clip [ECO-499534]. Rev B passes NVH [TR-280209] but cracks at the clip in the −40 °C impact test [TR-976411].
- **HS-69933:** a vibration failure [TR-743930] led to thread locker [ECO-101588]. Rev B passes vibration [TR-578098] but fails flatness [TR-434504].

**Weaker version of the same pattern:** some parts failed a dimensional check on rev A and were fixed by loosening the tolerance. Their rev B now fails static strength or salt spray. Examples: BK-56396 [TR-281390], BK-65148 [TR-799852], BD-60031 [TR-556159], PL-66349 [TR-639525], FL-82974 [TR-532575].
